terra.problem: The claim that livestock was a big deal for a man like Abram adds an unsupported fact about his circumstances.

Saying the house goes to the servant turns Abram's expectation about his heir into a fact. God says the servant will not be his heir. The explanation also supplies a reason Abram speaks plainly that the text does not give.
The passage does not say Abram is standing in the dark when God shows him the stars.
The claim that sand appears later in Abraham's story needs a reference outside this passage.
The passage does not say Abram lived with animals. That detail needs support from a referenced passage.
The passage does not say tents were everywhere in Abram's world or mention a camp in this scene.
The claim that Abram builds altars elsewhere needs a reference outside this passage.
The explanation is generic and flat: it gives the verse and restates the answer without much of Papa Dorin's voice.
The text says Abram drove the birds away, not that they did not get anything before he did.
The claim that people are scattered elsewhere in the Bible needs a reference.
Calling the news about Abram's descendants exile goes beyond the text, which says they will be strangers, enslaved and mistreated in another land.
The claim that Abram receives a new name later needs a reference outside this passage.
